subject: Energy
title: Sodium-Ion Batteries
description: A fast breakdown of Sodium-Ion Batteries for builders.

hook.text: Sodium-ion batteries use abundant sodium instead of lithium—potentially cutting costs and supply chain risks.

buildup.text: Sodium is 1,000 times more abundant than lithium—found in ordinary salt, available everywhere on Earth.

discovery.text: They work similarly to lithium-ion—sodium ions shuttle between electrodes, storing and releasing energy.

twist.text: Energy density is lower than lithium—but for stationary grid storage where weight doesn't matter, that's fine.

climax.text: CATL began mass-producing sodium-ion cells in 2023—the first major manufacturer to commercialize the technology.

punchline.text: Salt instead of lithium—cheaper batteries from common elements.

quiz.question: Why are sodium-ion batteries attractive for grid storage?
